topic: Can MVDR beamforming sufficiently compensate for pattern degradation in array-fed reflectors during element failures?
consensus_response: MVDR beamforming can sufficiently compensate for pattern degradation in array-fed reflectors during element failures, but its effectiveness is degraded by phase errors. The defocused reflector concept exhibits robustness against feed failures due to its bent feed array design, reducing defocusing effects and gain loss (1.52 dB). Adaptive calibration techniques can mitigate phase errors and improve MVDR's effectiveness. A more general approach could be the optimization of the reflector surface together with the feed array, potentially enhancing robustness against feed failures.
